_readme: Complete data example for build_docs.py. Keys starting with _ are ignored. Lesson hours (theory / practice / assessment) are the only source of numbers; the script sums them up to modules and the program. total_hours is optional and only used as a cross-check.
program_title: TRAINING PROGRAM: PACKAGING AND PUBLISHING AN ONLINE COURSE ON UDEMY
target_learners: Teachers, lecturers, tutors, corporate trainers, coaches and mentors who want to turn what they already teach into a complete video course and publish it themselves on Udemy.
Learners need a computer with Internet access and basic word processing and presentation skills. No experience in video production or online selling is required.
general_objective: Equip learners with the competencies needed to design and produce digital learning materials, package a course, and publish an online course that passes Udemy's quality review, based on a sound digital instructional design process and the regulations that apply to selling digital content.

knowledge: Describe digital teaching and learning, the main online learning models, and where a Udemy course sits among them;
Describe the online course design process and the structure of a digital course;
State the design principles for text, image, audio and video learning materials and the structure of a lecture video;
Describe the Udemy upload process, its review requirements, and the rules on copyright, personal data and tax that apply to selling online courses.
skills: Write learning objectives with Bloom's taxonomy and select and structure digital content for a topic in their own field;
Design a lecture slide deck using a Slide Master and presentation design principles;
Record and edit lecture videos with interaction points that meet Udemy's audio and video quality requirements;
Write a teaching script, package and test a complete course;
Upload, configure and submit the course for review on the Udemy Instructor Dashboard.
autonomy: Plan and complete their own course product on schedule;
Comply with copyright, platform terms and the law when publishing and selling digital content.

modules.title: Overview of online course design and packaging
modules.position: The first module of the program. It is the foundation for the materials design and packaging modules that follow.
modules.nature: A required foundation module on digital teaching. It gives learners the full picture of the process and the structure of an online course before production starts.

knowledge: Describe digital teaching and learning, blended learning, hybrid learning, the flipped classroom, online learning and distance learning, and where a Udemy course sits among them;
Describe the online course design process, the structure of a teaching plan and the structure of a digital course.
objectives.skills: Draw a structure map of a digital course for a topic in their own field with all five components: course information, activity instructions, learning materials, interaction, assessment.
objectives.autonomy: Choose a course topic that fits their own expertise and their learners' needs.

lessons.title: Digital teaching and online courses

objectives.knowledge: Describe digital teaching and learning, why it matters and what influences it; distinguish blended learning, hybrid learning, the flipped classroom, online learning and distance learning.
objectives.skills: Select the online learning model that fits one of their own teaching topics and locate a Udemy course within that model.
objectives.autonomy: Survey Udemy courses in the same field on their own initiative to position their course.

content: 1. Digital teaching and learning
1.1. Definition and components
1.2. Why digital teaching is needed and what influences it
2. Models and forms of digital teaching
2.1. Blended learning, hybrid learning, flipped classroom
2.2. Online learning, distance learning
3. Where a Udemy course sits in the online learning model
4. Discussion: choose the model that fits your own topic.
overview: Why digital teaching is needed and what influences it
Blended, hybrid, flipped classroom, online and distance learning
Where a Udemy course sits in the online learning model

lessons.title: The online course design process

objectives.knowledge: Describe the steps of the online course design process, the structure of a teaching plan (objectives, activities, assessment) and the structure of a digital course.
objectives.skills: Draw a structure map of a digital course for the chosen topic that has all 5 components and skips no step of the process.
objectives.autonomy: Follow the process without skipping the objective-setting and assessment steps.

content: 1. The online course design process
2. Structure of a teaching plan: learning objectives, teaching activities, assessment methods
3. Structure of a digital course: course and lesson information, activity instructions, learning materials, interaction, assessment
4. Practice: draw the structure map of your own digital course.
overview: Structure of a teaching plan: objectives, activities, assessment
Structure of a digital course: information, instructions, materials, interaction, assessment

conditions.learning_space: Self-paced online video. Learners need a quiet place and a computer with Internet access.
conditions.materials: Lecture videos, slides, a downloadable course structure map template, a list of reference Udemy courses.
conditions.other_resources: The Udemy Teaching Center course creation guidelines.

content.knowledge: Digital teaching, online learning models, the design process and the structure of a digital course.
content.autonomy: Initiative in choosing a topic and submitting the map on time.

assessment.method: Formative assessment through one submitted assignment (the course structure map) scored with a checklist. No end-of-module test.

guidelines.scope: For all learners of the program, whatever subject they teach.
guidelines.instructor: Teach in short videos of 5 to 10 minutes, illustrated with real Udemy courses in education; provide the map template; give feedback on submissions through Q&A.
guidelines.learners: Watch the videos, read the materials, survey 3 Udemy courses in their field, then draw and submit their own course structure map.
key_points: Telling the online learning models apart correctly;
A digital course structure with all 5 components.

references: Udemy, Teaching Center: course creation guidelines, https://teach.udemy.com/.

modules.title: Defining objectives and content for a digital course
modules.position: Delivered after M01 and before the materials design modules.
modules.nature: A required module that integrates knowledge of learning objectives with the skill of structuring content. Learners leave with an objectives and content design that drives all later production.

knowledge: Describe Bloom's taxonomy (2001 revision) and the action verbs of each level;
Describe the characteristics of digital teaching content and the steps for defining it.
skills: Write objectives for the course and for each lesson using the correct Bloom action verbs;
Collect, select, structure and refine the digital teaching content of their own course.
objectives.autonomy: Review and revise their own objectives and content in response to feedback.

lessons.title: Writing digital learning objectives with Bloom's taxonomy

objectives.knowledge: State the 6 cognitive levels of Bloom's 2001 taxonomy and the action verb group of each.
objectives.skills: Write at least 3 objectives for the course and 1 for each lesson, each starting with a measurable action verb at the intended level.
objectives.autonomy: Take care to remove unmeasurable verbs (understand, know, grasp) from their objectives.

content: 1. Bloom's taxonomy: concept and cognitive levels (2001 revision)
2. Writing learning objectives with the action verbs of each level
3. Practice: write course objectives and lesson objectives for the chosen topic.

lessons.title: Defining digital teaching content

objectives.knowledge: Explain partial and full virtualization of face-to-face teaching and the steps for defining digital teaching content.
objectives.skills: Build a content table for the course following the 4 steps (collect, select, structure, refine), with every content item tied to an objective.
objectives.autonomy: Cut content that does not serve an objective, on their own judgment.

content: 1. Characteristics of digital teaching content: partial and full virtualization of face-to-face teaching
2. Steps for defining digital teaching content: collect, select, structure, refine
3. Practice: build the content table for your own course.

conditions.materials: Bloom verb table (download), objectives table template, digital content table template.
conditions.other_resources: The course structure map produced in M01.

content.knowledge: Bloom's taxonomy and action verbs; the steps for defining digital teaching content.
content.skills: The objectives table and the content table of the learner's course.

assessment.method: End-of-module assessment combining an objective test on Bloom's taxonomy with a submitted assignment (objectives and content tables) scored with a checklist.

guidelines.scope: For all learners of the program.
guidelines.instructor: Show badly written and well written objectives taken from real education courses; provide the verb table; have learners score each other's objectives.
guidelines.learners: Watch the videos, take the quiz, write and submit the objectives table and the content table for their course.
key_points: Every objective opens with a measurable action verb;
Every content item traces back to an objective.

references: Anderson, L. W., Krathwohl, D. R. (2001), A Taxonomy for Learning, Teaching, and Assessing: A Revision of Bloom's Taxonomy of Educational Objectives, Longman.

modules.title: Designing text and image learning materials
modules.nature: A required module that integrates knowledge of digital learning materials with slide design skills. Learners produce the lecture slide deck used in their videos.

knowledge: Describe the concept, characteristics, formats and interaction types of text and image learning materials;
State presentation design principles and the procedure for creating a Slide Master.
objectives.skills: Design the slide deck for one lesson of the course using a Slide Master, with all 5 slide groups (topic, objectives, outline, development, review) and in line with presentation design principles.
objectives.autonomy: Respect image and font licences when designing.

lessons.title: Concept, formats and interaction in text and image learning materials

objectives.knowledge: Describe the concept, the characteristics, the 4 formats and the 3 interaction types of text and image learning materials.
objectives.skills: Select a format and an interaction type for each lesson of their course and justify the choice.
objectives.autonomy: Compare with materials from existing Udemy courses on their own initiative.

content: 1. Concept and characteristics of text and image learning materials
2. Formats: slide decks, digitized books and documents, lecture notes, worksheets
3. Interaction types: hyperlinks, navigation menus, acting on content (fill in the blank, multiple choice)
4. Practice: choose a format and interaction type for each lesson of your course.

lessons.title: Presentation design principles and the Slide Master

objectives.knowledge: State the presentation design principles and the procedure for creating a Slide Master.
objectives.skills: Create a Slide Master for the course with consistent layout, colours and fonts that serves at least 3 slide types.
objectives.autonomy: Keep the visual identity consistent across the course.

content: 1. Presentation design principles
2. Procedure for creating a Slide Master
3. Practice: create the Slide Master for your course.

lessons.title: Practice: designing lecture slides

objectives.knowledge: Describe the function of the 5 slide groups in a lecture.
objectives.skills: Design a complete slide deck for one lesson following the 5 steps, using the Slide Master, with no spelling errors and all images properly licensed.
objectives.autonomy: Check the deck against the checklist before submitting.

content: 1. Step 1: design the topic slide
2. Step 2: design the objectives slide
3. Step 3: design the outline slide
4. Step 4: design the content development slides
5. Step 5: design the review, check and closing slides

conditions.equipment: Computer with PowerPoint, Google Slides or Canva; Internet.
conditions.materials: Sample Slide Master, presentation design checklist, royalty-free image sources.
conditions.other_resources: The objectives and content tables produced in M02.

content.knowledge: Concept, formats and interaction of text and image materials; presentation principles.
content.skills: A complete slide deck for one lesson.
content.autonomy: Licence compliance and self-checking against the checklist.

assessment.method: End-of-module assessment by product: the slide deck is scored with a rubric.

guidelines.scope: For all learners of the program.
guidelines.instructor: Record the screen step by step; show a sample deck before and after revision; give feedback on each learner's deck.
guidelines.learners: Follow the videos, design the deck for their own lesson, score it with the checklist, submit.
key_points: All 5 slide groups in the right order.

references: Reynolds, G. (2019), Presentation Zen: Simple Ideas on Presentation Design and Delivery, 3rd ed., New Riders.

modules.title: Designing audio and video learning materials
modules.nature: A required module that integrates knowledge of multimedia materials with recording and editing skills. Learners produce lecture videos that meet Udemy's requirements.

knowledge: Describe the concept, characteristics, production formats and interaction types of audio and video learning materials;
State the design principles and the structure of a lecture video.
objectives.skills: Record and edit a 5 to 10 minute lecture video from the slides already designed, with interaction points, clear audio and sharp picture as required by Udemy's review.
objectives.autonomy: Persist in re-recording and re-editing until the quality standard is met.

lessons.title: Concept, formats and interaction in audio and video learning materials

objectives.knowledge: Describe the concept, the characteristics, the 3 production formats and the 3 interaction types of audio and video learning materials.
objectives.skills: Select a production format (slides to video, images to video, camera recording) for each lesson of the course and justify it.
objectives.autonomy: Weigh their own equipment constraints when choosing.

content: 1. Concept and characteristics of audio and video learning materials
2. Production formats: slides converted to video; images converted to video; camera or screen recording
3. Interaction types: questions inserted between segments; control menus; combining materials into a chain of learning activities
4. Practice: choose a production format for each lesson of your course.

lessons.title: Design principles and structure of a lecture video

objectives.knowledge: State the video design principles and the opening, body and closing structure of a lecture video.
objectives.skills: Write the video script for one lesson following that structure, marking where interactions go, for a planned length of 5 to 10 minutes.
objectives.autonomy: Limit video length on their own discipline.

content: 1. Video design principles
2. Structure of a lecture video
3. Practice: write the video script for one lesson.

lessons.title: Practice: recording and editing a lecture video

objectives.knowledge: Describe the preparation steps before recording and the basic editing operations.
objectives.skills: Record and edit one lecture video from the written script: clear audio without noise, sharp picture, illustrative slides inserted, at least 1 interaction point, within the planned length.
objectives.autonomy: Check the product against Udemy's quality criteria before submitting.

content: 1. Preparing to record: lighting, sound, framing, checking slides and script
2. Recording from the script; editing: cutting, inserting slides and images, inserting interaction points

conditions.equipment: Computer, microphone, webcam or phone, screen recording and video editing software (OBS, Camtasia, CapCut or equivalent).
conditions.materials: Video script template, audio and video quality checklist based on Udemy's requirements.
conditions.other_resources: The slide deck produced in M03.

content.knowledge: Concept, formats and interaction of audio and video materials; principles and structure of a lecture video.
content.skills: A complete lecture video for one lesson.
content.autonomy: Self-checking and correction against the quality criteria.

assessment.method: End-of-module assessment by product: the lecture video is scored with a rubric.

guidelines.scope: For all learners of the program.
guidelines.instructor: Demonstrate equipment setup and editing on screen; show videos that passed and failed review; give feedback on each submitted video.
guidelines.learners: Write the script, record, edit, check against the checklist, submit the video.
key_points: Audio is the first thing Udemy rejects a course for;
The video has a structure and interaction points.

references: Mayer, R. E. (2021), Multimedia Learning, 3rd ed., Cambridge University Press.
Udemy, Course quality checklist, Udemy Teaching Center, https://teach.udemy.com/.

sections.heading: 1.1. Admission
items: Admit learners who match section I. There is no cap on numbers because the program runs online.
Learners who already have a published Udemy course may be exempted from M05 and M06 on presenting evidence.

sections.heading: 1.2. Delivery
items: The program is delivered fully online as a self-paced video course on Udemy, with Q&A and submitted assignments.
Lesson time is video watching time (theory) plus time spent following along and doing assignments (practice, discussion). Learners set their own pace. Completion within 6 weeks is recommended.
The provider needs a Udemy instructor account, a way to manage submissions and a feedback turnaround of 7 days.

sections.heading: 1.3. Assessment and certification
items: Learners are assessed on a module once they have watched at least 80% of its videos and submitted all its assignments. End-of-module assessments are scored on a 10-point scale. Below 5.0 the product is resubmitted.
The final program score is the rubric score of the complete Udemy course (M08). The other modules are prerequisites.

Learners who complete 100% of the content receive Udemy's certificate of completion. Learners with a rubric score of 5.0 or higher also receive the provider's certificate, graded Excellent 9.0 to 10, Very good 8.0 to under 9.0, Good 7.0 to under 8.0, Pass 5.0 to under 7.0.

sections.heading: 1.4. Recognition of prior learning
items: Learners who have completed a recognized digital teaching module in a teacher training program may be exempted from M01 and M02.

implementation_guidelines.heading: 2. Requirements for the training provider
items: The instructor has published at least one Udemy course that passed review and has teaching qualifications.
All materials, templates, checklists and rubrics named in the modules are available. Screen recordings are updated when the Udemy interface changes.
The provider uses this program as the basis for writing or selecting materials suited to online delivery.
